Experience handling animal models and behavioral training protocols
Experience with maintaining institutional regulatory and safety compliance
Previous experience working in a research setting, including basic laboratory procedures and managing day-to-day laboratory logistics

The Staff Research Associate (SRA) will support NIH-sponsored research projects in hearing-related neuroscience and auditory prostheses, including preclinical studies of cochlear implant technologies. Primary responsibilities include conducting routine behavioral testing, performing non-invasive electrophysiological measurements, and assisting with extracellular neural recording experiments. These duties require handling and training non-rodent animal models in operant-based perceptual tasks; proficiency in auditory electrophysiological recording techniques; and preparing and administering veterinary medications and experimental agents.

The SRA will also provide perioperative support for survival and acute laboratory surgeries. These duties include preparing the operating space, pharmaceuticals, and sterile instruments; assisting with intraoperative procedures and health monitoring; and executing postoperative care

protocols. The SRA will maintain accurate research records, help with data management, and utilize programming environments such as MATLAB or Python, with opportunities to contribute to quantitative data analysis. Additionally, the SRA will support routine laboratory operations,

including inventory management and procurement, general lab maintenance, coordinating with veterinary staff to manage animal welfare, and ensuring compliance with university and federal regulatory guidelines. Prior experience with the above-mentioned techniques is advantageous, but supplemental training will be provided.
Basic proficiency using MATLAB or Python

Due to the nature of the experiments, this position will require scheduling flexibility, including occasional work on weekends or during evening hours. The candidate must be willing to work with animals. All studies will be conducted in accordance with the National Institute of Health guidelines and with the approval of the UCI Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee.
Familiarity with electrophysiological recording techniques
Skills in formulating and administering veterinary medications and providing surgical support (e.g., aseptic technique, health monitoring)
Ability to manage detailed research records and data pipelines
Demonstrated ability to work independently
